rationale: Both observed decode windows selected w4d<2,1,4,2,1>, with 128 calls and 9.09–9.11 ms of device time per step. This profile's adjacent four lanes held identical 128-bit row headers. A lane now holds one 32-bit word of each header, reconstructs its group's header via width-four register shuffles, prepares one of four subblock scale/minimum pairs and broadcasts the actual rounded half2 bits. A single superblock stays in registers while a warp prefetches the next in-bounds quant region into L2. One byte permutation for each pair of quant bytes supplies both nibble planes. The high-nibble conversion (1024+16*q)/16-64 is exact in half precision for all unsigned four-bit integers. The subsequent scale FMA, tensor-core operations and accumulation order are identical. Warp liveness, K bounds and the unrolled subblock loop are uniform within a warp. The original tile clamp and output mask cover partial rows. The ABI, dispatch table, packed weights and served work are unchanged. A local sm_80 NVRTC/ptxas 12.6 compile of this specialization reduced registers from 236 to 168 with zero spills in both. The steady-state backward branch encloses 828 static SASS instructions for one superblock, versus 1,755 for two in the reference. Static code metrics do not establish throughput. Historical PS and shared staging did poorly at 32, so this reuses the packed on-device representation. Losing register lookahead and increased shuffle traffic can still offset the savings; the paired target serving tests decide.
